site.title: Sandeep Mishra | Product Security Engineer
site.description: Sandeep Mishra is a Senior Associate Product Security Engineer at MathWorks India. He works on application security and penetration testing, and has built Android, web and cross-platform apps.

profile.name: Sandeep Mishra
profile.title: Senior Associate Product Security Engineer
profile.intro: I work on product and application security at MathWorks. Before that, and alongside it, I have built Android, web and backend apps, and I like building tools that make security testing easier.

paragraphs: I'm a Senior Associate Product Security Engineer at MathWorks India with a background in Software Development and a degree in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from IIT Patna.

My current work primarily focuses on product and application security. I perform security assessments and hands-on penetration testing across multiple web applications, including assessments supporting SOC 2 Type II reviews. This involves understanding application functionality, identifying security weaknesses, reviewing areas such as API design and access control, and working with development teams to address security issues.

I've also been developing AI-assisted workflows to support application security assessments. The idea is to combine automation, security tools, and manual validation to make parts of the testing process more efficient and repeatable. I'm particularly interested in exploring how AI agents can assist with security analysis without taking away the importance of human validation and practical testing.

Alongside my security work, I've spent considerable time developing applications across Android, web, and backend technologies. Some of the projects I've worked on include Highway Watch, an Android application developed for Manipur Police to support highway patrolling through real-time vehicle tracking and a web-based monitoring panel, and Shield Pass, a cross-platform password manager built using Kotlin Multiplatform and the MERN stack.

I also worked on an Android security project with the Indian Army, focusing on malware analysis and reverse engineering. This involved studying Android malware, performing static and dynamic analysis, monitoring network traffic, and modifying application code using Smali.
More recently, I've been building CyberVM-AI, a project exploring reproducible penetration-testing environments and the integration of local and cloud-based LLMs into security workflows.

I enjoy working at the intersection of software development and cybersecurity, whether that means understanding how an application is built, finding security weaknesses, or building tools that make security testing easier. I'm always interested in learning new technologies and exploring practical security challenges.

projects.name: CyberVM-AI
projects.tagline: A reproducible, AI-assisted penetration-testing lab on Kali Linux
points: Set up a Kali penetration-testing lab with Ansible, VirtualBox and Bash. Each engagement gets a fresh, disposable VM, and the toolchain (including Burp Suite and Playwright MCP) is version-controlled and checksum-verified.
Connected local and cloud LLMs through OpenCode, with a FastAPI and Qdrant RAG service that pulls in NVD, CISA KEV, EPSS and MITRE ATT&CK data.
Kept the lab contained with network isolation, host firewall allow-listing, and credentials that are only injected at runtime.

projects.name: Shield Pass
projects.tagline: Password manager for Android, iOS, desktop and web
points: Built Shield Pass with Kotlin Compose Multiplatform, so one codebase runs on Android, iOS and desktop.
Protected saved passwords with dual authentication (a login PIN and an app PIN), AES encryption and Blake2b hashing, with encrypted cloud sync across devices. Biometric login is planned.
Used Jetpack Compose and its WindowSize class so the layout adapts to phones, tablets and desktop screens.
Built the web version with the MERN stack (React, Express, Node.js, MongoDB).
Deployed the web app on Render (with a cron job to keep it awake), the Android app on the Play Store and the Windows app on GitHub Releases.

Used Firebase to store and serve the live location data.
Built a web panel to watch live locations and look through location logs.

articles.title: How I Solved the Indian Army Terrier Cyber Quest 2026 Web Challenges
articles.summary: A walkthrough of how I solved three web challenges from Terrier Cyber Quest 2026: prototype pollution past a WAF in a Node.js app, a SQL injection login bypass where the checks only ran in the browser, and getting around a keyword-based SQL injection filter.
